sections.summary: Articles are words that define nouns as specific or unspecific. English has two types: definite (the) and indefinite (a/an).
rules: Use "the" for specific nouns or when something is mentioned again
No article for plural/uncountable nouns in general statements
examples: I saw a dog. The dog was brown. (first mention → specific)
The sun rises in the east. (unique things)
I like coffee. (general - no article with uncountable)

commonMistakes.explanation: Student starts with consonant sound /st/, use "a"
No article when referring to the general purpose (education)

quiz.question: She is ___ honest person.
quiz.explanation: Honest starts with vowel sound /ɒ/, use "an"

quiz.question: I love ___ music.
quiz.explanation: General statements with uncountable nouns need no article

sections.summary: Prepositions show relationships between nouns and other words. The most common are in, on, at.
rules: Place: at (specific points), on (surfaces), in (enclosed spaces)
at: at 3 PM, at night, at home, at the door
on: on Monday, on the table, on the wall
in: in May, in 2020, in the morning, in the room
examples: I wake up at 7 AM. (specific time)
The book is on the table. (surface)
He lives in New York. (city/enclosed space)

commonMistakes.wrong: I will see you in Monday.
commonMistakes.correct: I will see you on Monday.
commonMistakes.explanation: Use "on" with days of the week

commonMistakes.wrong: The class starts at the morning.
commonMistakes.correct: The class starts in the morning.
commonMistakes.explanation: Use "in" with parts of the day (except "at night")

quiz.question: The party is ___ Saturday night.
quiz.explanation: Use "on" with specific days and nights of the week

sections.summary: Modal verbs express ability, permission, obligation, advice, or possibility.
rules: Modal + base form (no "to" except ought to)

commonMistakes.explanation: Modal verbs are followed by base form without "to"
Modal verbs don't add -s in third person

quiz.question: You ___ eat so much sugar. It's unhealthy.
I ___ finish this project by Friday.
